problem: Exploit video-diffusion temporal representations for action prediction without the latency of generating full videos at every control step.
contribution: VidMan first learns video prediction, then adapts intermediate features into a supervised implicit inverse-action policy with layer-wise adapters. It uses one video-backbone pass at maximal noise and a smaller iterative action diffusion head.
algorithm: Initialize OpenSora16x256x256; train twohistory/twofuture-frame generation on robot videos with channel-concatenated history and text. In stage2 insert gated attention/FFN adapters with learned action queries after each backboneblock. Fix video timestepK=1000 and use pure future noise; no video denoising loop. Decode action queries with100-step diffusion actionhead; stage2 action-only objective outperforms joint frame/actiontraining.
observations: Stage1third-personRGB;stage2third-person+wrist and optionalproprioception. Four-frame sampling interval3 is a tuned design. Prediction features encode learned priors, not measured future states or independently verified dynamics.
actions: Target EEFpose/gripper controls;12actionsteps forOXE and10forCALVIN. Requires target action supervision; pretrained features do not calibrate motorjoints or gripper polarity.
